subject: Mental Models
title: Fishbone Diagram
description: A micro-lesson that makes Fishbone Diagram usable.

hook.text: Kaoru Ishikawa drew a fish skeleton on a whiteboard. Each bone represented a category of causes.

buildup.text: The fishbone diagram organizes possible causes into branches: people, process, materials, machines, environment.

discovery.text: By filling in each branch, teams discover causes they would have overlooked. Visual structure prevents tunnel vision.

twist.text: The diagram does not identify the cause. It maps the search space.

climax.text: Use the fishbone to brainstorm broadly, then use evidence to narrow.

punchline.text: Draw the fish first. Data picks the bone.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of a fishbone diagram?
options: To organize possible causes into categories and prevent tunnel vision
